### To replicate
(Based on the instructions from https://docs.yugabyte.com/latest/manage/backup-restore/snapshots-ycql/)

#### 1. Create a new cluster
```
./bin/yb-ctl destroy && ./bin/yb-ctl create
```

#### 2. Connect with `ycqlsh` and set up a table

```
./bin/ycqlsh
```

```
CREATE KEYSPACE ydb;
use ydb;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ydb.test_tb(k int primary key, v1 int, v2 int, v3 int) with transactions = {'enabled' : true};
CREATE INDEX test_db_idx on ydb.test_tb(v1);
insert into test_tb(k, v1, v2, v3) values (1,2,3,4);
select * from test_tb;
```
```

 k | v1 | v2 | v3
---+----+----+----
 1 |  2 |  3 |  4

(1 rows)
```

#### 3. Set up the snapshot

```
./bin/yb-admin create_snapshot ydb test_tb
./bin/yb-admin list_snapshots
```
```
I0720 00:00:20.807389 112762304 mem_tracker.cc:249] MemTracker: hard memory limit is 13.600000 GB
I0720 00:00:20.807937 112762304 mem_tracker.cc:251] MemTracker: soft memory limit is 11.560000 GB
I0720 00:00:20.808691 112762304 thread_pool.cc:166] Starting thread pool { name: yb-admin queue_limit: 10000 max_workers: 1024 }
I0720 00:00:20.809301 112762304 client-internal.cc:1947] New master addresses: [localhost:7100]
W0720 00:00:20.814528 57233408 dns_resolver.cc:149] Peer address 'localhost' resolves to [127.0.0.1, ::1] different addresses. Using 127.0.0.1
W0720 00:00:20.839041 57769984 dns_resolver.cc:149] Peer address 'localhost' resolves to [127.0.0.1, ::1] different addresses. Using 127.0.0.1
Snapshot UUID                    	State
242b53f1-c141-4c38-a254-70a6c58a0185 	COMPLETE
```

#### 4. Export and Import the snapshot
Using the snapshot uuid returned above do 
```
./bin/yb-admin export_snapshot <snapshot-uuid> test_tb.snapshot
```
Then just
```
./bin/yb-admin import_snapshot test_tb.snapshot test_ybd test_tb
```
_Note: we don't actually need the data to cause the crash so skipping the snapshot copy steps._

#### 5. Test the index in `ycqlsh`:
Query using just the table will work (but return no rows because we skipped the data copy step).
```
select * from test_ybd.test_tb;
```
```
 k | v1 | v2 | v3
---+----+----+----

(0 rows)
```

Query using the index will crash.

```
select * from test_ybd.test_tb where v1 = 1;
```
```
NoHostAvailable:
```

### Possible cause
The root issue seems to be that the restored index does not have the mangled column names (e.g. `C$_v1`) but rather the user-level names (`v1`) -- though that may not be the only issue. We checked that the exported data in `test_tb.snapshot` contains the correct names, so the issue is likely on the restore path.
Exported pbs:
```
bin/yb-pbc-dump test_tb.snapshot
```
